# Provided CPU project

`submission/run.py` is the CLI entry; `formats.py` validates the request envelope.
`pipeline.py` connects offline discovery to deployment/session processing.
`offline_discovery/rule_generate.py` contains packet-segment extraction, distance,
clustering and range-representation code. `rule_remove.py` contains coverage and
filtering code. `online_matching/match_p4.py` contains the batch classifier and
model loading. `train_rf.py` contains the CPU backup-tree training path.

The current batch code is an incomplete starting point for PROTOCOL.md. Its
historical sample length, activation/window, floating score, filtering and
priority behavior are not authority over the contract. Session and release-bank
integration must be completed. You may change/reorganize project modules and add
regular source/config files within the published bounds. No file-by-file patch
shape or particular implementation layout is graded. The complete functional
certificate/replay contract is the authority.

The provided binary wheels are prepared offline by `prepare_env.py`; the public
checker runs this automatically. No TensorFlow, packet-capture reader, GPU or
switch installation is needed in this post-inference profile. Linux x86_64 and
CPython3.11.14 with the supplied CPU package versions are the target runtime.
Repair the provided Synecdoche discovery-to-deployment project.
Work in `/workspace/submission`; `run.py` is the JSON stdin/stdout entry point.
Extend its real offline discovery, calibration, backup and matching components.
Produce exact fragment, cluster, score, backup-tree and table certificates.
Replay atomic installs and interleaved flow epochs across model releases.
Account for range/exact banks retained by open flows, including classified ones.
Preserve the specified direction, priority, fallback and release-lifetime rules.
Read `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md` for complete schemas, arithmetic and boundaries.
`PROJECT.md` describes the supplied modules and offline CPU environment.
The pinned CPU packages and all installation files are already supplied locally.
No neural training, packet capture, network access or switch hardware is needed.
Return one complete JSON response; invalid requests return the specified error.
Submit the whole project with `run.py`, within the documented file/byte bounds.
Other regular project files are allowed; documented development caches are ignored.
Run `python3 check.py submission` from `/workspace` as a nonroot user.
The command prepares local wheels automatically and runs small public sanity cases.
All requirements apply beyond those cases; the public checker gives no score.
Your implementation must handle the whole published request budget in one process.
